result.rationale: The diff shows limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i in groups_controller.rb members action, with no upper bound before members.limit(limit). A caller can pass limit=10000000 and force serialization of all group members in one request. This is a substantive review concern grounded in the new pagination code (missing ceiling/validation), but the mechanism functions as designed — it's a missing safeguard, not broken behavior, so it fits important_non_bug.

judged_text: The new pagination contract accepts an unbounded limit ((params[:limit] || 50).to_i with no ceiling), so ?limit=10000000 still materializes and serializes every member of the group in one request. Any caller who can see the group can force a full join scan plus full serialization of all members in one request — the unbounded path this pagination was introduced to remove remains reachable.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new pagination params are taken as `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` with no upper bound, and then used directly in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` and serialized (`serialize_data(members, GroupUserSerializer)`). This makes `?limit=10000000` capable of fetching/serializing the entire group membership (up to total), undermining the pagination goal and enabling a large, expensive request by any caller allowed through `guardian.ensure_can_see!`.
